messages.text:
Hi Allie — Jordan asked me to pass something on to you.

He told me yesterday that things between him and Sarah have been awkward lately, and that for now he'd rather not see her outside of work. He asked me to let you know, since you're often the one hosting get-togethers — so you can plan around it.

That's as much as he told me; if you want details, better to ask him directly.
Thanks for passing that on, Dana. I'll keep it in mind when I plan things — and I'll ask Jordan directly about the details rather than making you the middleman.

Hey Jordan — Dana passed on that you'd rather not see Sarah outside of work for now, and that I should plan around it. Thanks for getting the word to me. Just so I get it right: should I keep the two of you apart in anything I organize, or would you rather I leave the planning to you two? Happy to hear it from you directly whenever you want to talk.

Thanks for checking with me directly, Allie — I appreciate it. Yes, for now I'd rather not be at the same things as Sarah outside work: if you're organizing something, just don't put the two of us in the same plan. No drama about it, and nothing needs to change at the department. Happy to talk it through whenever.
Got it, and thanks for saying it plainly. I won't put you and Sarah in the same plan for now; everything at the department stays as it is. Nothing else to sort out on my side — talk whenever.

Hey Allie! Random idea — would you be up for hosting a little get-together at your place this Saturday, around 3:30? Nothing fancy, just people hanging out.

And if you're in: could you ask Jordan to come? Just invite him yourself, like it's your own thing — I'd rather my name not come into it. Things have been a bit awkward between us lately and I don't want him to feel like it's about me.

No pressure at all, just say if it works.

Hey Sarah — Saturday 3:30 works, I'm happy to host. Nothing fancy is exactly my kind of get-together.

One thing though: I can't invite Jordan under a cover story. He told me directly that he'd rather not be at the same out-of-work plans as you for now, and inviting him while hiding who it's for would go against what he asked me. I'd rather not put either of you in that spot.

So how about this: Saturday stands, and I'll gather whoever else wants to come. And if you want Jordan there, the ask should come from you — you said yourself you'd rather he didn't feel it was about you, and honestly a direct word from you is the only version of that which isn't me managing it behind his back. I'm glad to help with anything else around it.

Thanks Allie — and you're right, I shouldn't have asked you to do it that way. Cover story's off the table; I won't put you in that spot.

So: Saturday 3:30 at yours, count me in, and I'll write to Jordan myself and ask him straight. If he says no, that's fine and I'll leave it.

Hey Jordan. Allie's hosting a small get-together at her place this Saturday around 3:30, and I'd like you there.

I know things have been a bit awkward between us lately, so I'd rather just say it plainly than have it come at you sideways. No pressure either way — if you'd rather skip it, that's genuinely fine.

Thanks for asking me straight, Sarah — I appreciate that. I'll pass on Saturday, though. I've been keeping things to work for a while, and I'd rather not change that just yet. Nothing against you; enjoy it.
Perfect — Saturday 3:30 at mine it is, and thanks for taking it that way. I'll get the place ready. Tell me if anything changes on your side.
Thanks for saying so, Jordan — no hard feelings at all. Door's open whenever you feel like it.
Will do. See you Saturday at 3:30 — and thanks for hosting.
